transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, so I guess what brings me in is that I'm having a lot of trouble at my job. I work at a meat processing plant, and I keep starting the sanitation steps, or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and somehow I just... leave out the last parts. Even when I know my job totally depends on finishing them correctly. 

It’s super strict there. Actually, the safety inspector came by last Tuesday and he was wearing these really weird neon green rubber boots. I remember staring at them thinking they looked like something out of a cartoon, like, who wears neon green on a processing floor? Usually everyone just wears the standard white ones they issue us in the locker room. I had to buy my own gel insoles for mine, though, because standing on that concrete all day is just brutal on your back. My roommate told me I should try yoga for that, since she started going to this studio downtown that does the hot yoga, but... wait, I'm sorry, I completely lost my train of thought. 

What was I saying? Oh, right, work. Yeah, I just keep leaving my logs and the end of the sanitation stuff unfinished, and I really need to stop doing that before I get fired.
Did you have this same kind of trouble with attention or finishing things when you were a child?

Yeah, definitely. Um, my mom actually still has some of my old report cards from, like, fourth grade? And they always said the same thing—that I was bright but I needed constant reminders to actually finish my classwork or turn in my homework. Which is funny because my mom kept everything. She has this huge plastic bin in her attic filled with all my old school stuff, and some of my brother's too, but mostly mine. She even kept this macaroni art thing I made in kindergarten that smells really weird now. I don't know why she holds onto that stuff, she's trying to downsize right now because she wants to move to Florida. She hates the winters here, which, honestly, I get. The snow just turns into that gross gray slush on the side of the road after two days anyway. 

But, um, yeah, as a kid... I remember I would understand the lessons totally fine, but I'd miss whole chunks of the instructions unless the teacher was, like, standing right next to me.
Do you have the same kind of trouble finishing things outside of work too?

Yeah, for sure. Like, my apartment is always a mess because of it. I'll start doing the laundry, right? And then I'll pull out a shirt that I bought back when I was getting my degree—I just finished my bachelor's, actually. But anyway, I got it at this amazing vintage thrift store near campus. The owner had this massive golden retriever that would just sleep right in the middle of the clothing racks, so you literally had to step over him to look at the jackets. I love dogs so much, but my current landlord has a super strict no-pet policy. It's really annoying because I feel like a cat would be great to have around, you know? My roommate really wants a cat too. She was looking at the animal shelter's website the other day and saw this orange tabby that was missing half an ear. It looked like a cute little pirate, and we were trying to figure out if we could sneak it past the landlord, but... wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, outside of work. Yeah, I just never actually finish folding the laundry or doing whatever chore I start at home either.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I feel anxious or on edge very much. Sometimes I get a little stressed when I realize I'm super behind on something, but it's not like a constant anxious feeling, you know? It's more just... being frustrated with myself. 

Actually, my roommate is the one who gets really anxious. She has this whole morning routine where she has to drink her coffee out of this specific mug that has a little ceramic frog sitting at the bottom of it. She got it at a pottery class we took together last year. I was terrible at it, honestly. My bowl looked like a weird, lopsided lump of clay. But she made this really cool vase, and then she made that frog mug. She says if she doesn't use it, her whole day feels off. I don't really drink coffee, though. It makes my stomach feel weird. I prefer tea, like that chamomile stuff? I found this amazing loose-leaf tea shop downtown, right next to that hot yoga place I mentioned earlier. The owner there is so nice, she always gives me free samples of the new blends. Last time she gave me this peach-mango one that smelled exactly like those gummy rings you get at the gas station. I love those things, especially on road trips. I went on a road trip to Chicago once and... wait, sorry. What were we talking about? 

Oh, right. No, I don't really feel anxious or on edge. Just mostly distracted, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern of distractibility, losing train of thought, failing to complete tasks, and missing instructions across multiple settings (work, home, and childhood school functioning), with clear functional impairment at work and home. Symptoms began in childhood and persist into adulthood. Anxiety was denied as a primary explanation. This is most consistent with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation.
